title: Throttled
haiku:
They held the valve shut
no untested water flows
wisdom, for once, wins
headline: OpenAI declined to release its newest AI model, Astra, citing unresolved safety concerns.

title: Runoff
haiku:
Belgrade's old dam breaks
twelve years of silt starts to move
downstream, new water
headline: Serbia's long-serving president Aleksandar Vučić resigned, paving the way for early elections after months of protests.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Storm drains gasp, then flood
I sized these pipes for less rain
the sky forgot code
headline: A powerful nor'easter caused flooding across the northeastern US, prompting New York and New Jersey to declare states of emergency.

title: Unclogged
haiku:
The judge reopens
a valve the White House shut tight
the press flows again
headline: A federal court ordered the Trump administration to restore press access, blocking its ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House.

title: Backflow
haiku:
I've heard threats like these
yet the line still carries talk
old pipes, still some flow
headline: Trump threatened Iran with annihilation at the UN, yet the US and Iran held their first talks since June that same week.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Newsrooms shut the valve,
one signal, all outlets balk,
clean water still runs.
headline: Major U.S. news outlets boycotted a shared White House video feed of Trump in protest at new restrictions on the press pool.

title: Unclaimed
haiku:
No flag on the ice
just old friends drafting a deal
the map holds its line
headline: The US and Denmark reached a deal over Greenland, defusing Trump's earlier annexation threats.

title: Tributary
haiku:
Old allies reroute
round a wall no one can name
water finds its way
headline: The EU offered to make Canada an 'associate member' as both countries' ties to the U.S. grow strained.

title: Confluence
haiku:
Ballots where guns were
a channel dug through old war,
water finds its course
headline: Voters turned out for a landmark election in the Philippines' Muslim autonomous Bangsamoro region, a milestone in the decades-long peace process ending a separatist insurgency.

title: Leverage
haiku:
One valve, one desert
turns the whole world's pressure gauge
I taught men to flow
headline: Saudi Arabia shut a major oil pipeline after a drone attack launched from Iraq, part of the escalating standoff between Iran and the U.S.

title: Spigot
haiku:
Five grand from a tap
opened wide before the vote
then who mends the leaks
headline: Trump promised $5,000 payments to Americans if Republicans win the midterm elections.

title: Crudeness
haiku:
Oil pressure red-lines
old pipes groan toward war again—
I've patched worse than this
headline: Iran signaled readiness to escalate conflict with the U.S. as oil surged past $100 a barrel amid intensifying Middle East turmoil.

title: Shortfall
haiku:
Far right rises, short
one seat from the flood gate's edge
still the old seal holds
headline: Germany's far-right AfD won Saxony-Anhalt's state election but fell just short of the majority needed to govern alone.

title: Proportional
haiku:
Africa, unbent
the old map's thumb lifts at last
true scale, true weight, home
headline: The UN General Assembly voted to adopt a new world map correcting decades of projections that shrank Africa's true relative size.

title: Loaner
haiku:
A borrowed kidney
keeps filtering past the odds
the system still flows
headline: A genetically modified pig kidney has kept working inside a U.S. man's body for a record 271 days.

title: Undammed
haiku:
Born here, still it flows
a judge holds the old pipe true
bedrock outlasts men
headline: A federal judge blocked the Trump administration's second attempt to restrict birthright citizenship.

title: Buried
haiku:
Mud fills the tunnels
still we dig for the living
a thousand names lost
headline: Nepal's flood and landslide death toll has crossed 1,000, with rescuers racing to free workers trapped in mud-filled tunnels near the China border.

title: Backflow
haiku:
Calm month, then backflow
the oil climbs where pressure breaks
old valves still can hold
headline: The United States and Iran exchanged military strikes overnight, ending a month-long calm and sending global oil prices toward $90 a barrel as world finance officials meet.

title: Waterline
haiku:
Nepal's rivers rose
and swallowed a sleeping town
I have seen this rise
headline: Nepal's flash floods swept away a town, rescuers pulled survivors from a hydropower tunnel, and officials warned a glacial lake could breach and flood again.

title: Flushed
haiku:
Neighbors trade barbs north
the throne room short on tissue
even pipes need friends
headline: The US and Canada's trade war escalates with tariffs up to 50%, driving a surge in American toilet paper prices.

title: Unsanctioned
haiku:
Syria unlocked
off the terror list, at last
old pipes, new water
headline: The United States removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism.

title: Repressure
haiku:
Some pressure returns
in old pipes I thought were dry
the main still can flow
headline: Analysts say Democrats' chances of winning back the Senate are improving.

title: Backflow
haiku:
A judge cracks the valve
seventy-five nations' door
swings open again
headline: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration's visa ban on 75 countries was illegal.

title: Straitened
haiku:
Spain lifts an old gate
children cross the strait at last
a clogged pipe runs clear
headline: Spain reversed a policy that trapped migrant children in Ceuta, clearing the way for roughly 500 to move to the mainland.

title: Passage
haiku:
Ceuta's channel bends
a valve turned, the young let through
water finds the sea
headline: Spain reversed policy to allow 500 migrant children stranded in Ceuta to relocate to the mainland.

title: Clearance
haiku:
Small lungs, once clogged pipes,
we scrubbed the air and they cleared
I've seen pipes heal too.
headline: A study found children's lung function recovered faster than scientists expected after London's ultra-low emission zone cut air pollution.

title: Bedrock
haiku:
Foundations were poured
a judge rules the blueprints hold
no whim moves concrete
headline: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration cannot cancel the FBI's planned headquarters move to Maryland.

title: Unclogged
haiku:
Nine months in shadow
one American walks free
the pipe runs clear now
headline: An American missionary held captive in Niger for nine months has been freed.

title: Reflow
haiku:
Nine months in the pipe
the blockage clears, he walks out
water finds its way
headline: An American missionary kidnapped in Niger was freed after nine months in captivity.

title: Thaw
haiku:
I've seen this valve stuck
seventy years sealed—Seoul asks
let the current flow
headline: South Korea proposed formal talks to officially end the Korean War, more than seven decades after the armistice.

title: Aftershock
haiku:
Ground gave no warning
and swallowed a hundred homes
I light one candle
headline: A powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, killing well over a hundred people as rescuers search the rubble for survivors.

title: Setback
haiku:
Another blueprint
shelved before the concrete dries—
still, I mix more sand
headline: Israel rejected President Trump's 15-point plan to disarm Hamas in Gaza.

title: Backflow
haiku:
One valve did not break
though the current pushed, it held
clean water still flows
headline: The Senate let Trump's push for a new voting bill quietly die rather than pass it.

title: Opener
haiku:
Women take the field
history swings open wide
a door long rusted
headline: The Women's Professional Baseball League made its historic debut.

title: Unthrottled
haiku:
Missouri said no
to narrowing their own valve
the pipe stays open
headline: Missouri voters rejected a ballot measure that would have curtailed their own power to pass laws by initiative.

title: Overflow
haiku:
Fences choke the flow
a young life dammed at the shore
water finds a way
headline: A mass border crossing at Ceuta has plunged Moroccan migrants into despair and exposed deep divisions within Europe over how to respond.

title: Reflow
haiku:
A valve turned back on
vaccines flow to children's arms
the pipe remembers
headline: The U.S. restored some vaccine and health aid funding to UNICEF, Gavi, and the World Food Programme.

title: Spillway
haiku:
Rivers seek new banks
one skirmish floods a region
I've seen this spillway
headline: The U.S. launched fresh strikes on Iran, widening the war as it draws in Iraqi militias and other regional actors.

title: Throttled
haiku:
Two days, no new strike
some valve somewhere holds the line
and the crude runs calm
headline: The U.S. and Iran held off on strikes for a second straight day, and oil prices fell on the de-escalation.

title: Sluice
haiku:
Enough hands, one valve
turns, the old minister steps
down, current flows on
headline: India's education minister resigned, handing a win to student protesters who had organized against him.

title: Seepage
haiku:
Signal finds the crack
young hands raise their phones like pipes
truth still finds its grade
headline: Young protesters in India used smartphones to route around Modi government media controls and organize demonstrations.

title: Grounded
haiku:
Target the water
and the bridge that lifts the light
the grid always mends
headline: Trump threatened to strike Iran's bridges and power plants if attacks near the Strait of Hormuz continue.

title: Satirical
haiku:
a joke finds its spine
millions laughing turn to march—
the street clears its throat
headline: In India, a protest that began as satire grows into a nationwide challenge to Narendra Modi's government.

title: Removable
haiku:
no tanks in the street —
a moving van at Downing,
keys change hands by vote
headline: Andy Burnham replaces Keir Starmer as the United Kingdom's prime minister

title: Structural
haiku:
I taught men to build
bridges, pipelines, waterworks —
how quickly boys break
headline: Iran and US widen attacks as renewed conflict shows no sign of de-escalating

title: Sweepingly
haiku:
the sweepers come out
as they did in every war —
brooms outlast bombers
headline: Kyiv hit again as Ukraine reports two dead in Russian strike

title: Unfenced
haiku:
fences do come down —
I have lived long enough, twice,
to watch walls give up
headline: Gibraltar ushers in a new era as border fence with Spain is removed

title: Photogenic
haiku:
the summit's group shot:
smiles rowed up like clean fenceposts
smoke behind the lens
headline: US, Iran threaten more attacks as strikes continue, Trump attends NATO summit

title: Mortality
haiku:
I've buried strongmen
from my armchair, one by one —
the crowds weep; time won't
headline: Mourners throng funeral procession for Iran's supreme leader

title: Remembrance
haiku:
each name read aloud —
no nation is too broken
to remember well
headline: Venezuela quake death toll rises to 3,342 as families search for the missing

title: Anniversary
haiku:
two hundred fifty —
the oath still means what it says
even when we don't
headline: Nation celebrates 250th anniversary of American independence

title: Applause
haiku:
five days under stone
and the street still claps for one —
that's the whole species
headline: Venezuela earthquake death toll passes 1,700 as miraculous rescues offer hope

title: Signals
haiku:
two taps in the dark —
all our satellites, and still
hope travels by hand
headline: Survivors of Venezuela earthquakes found in rubble as death toll climbs past 1,400

title: Underdogs
haiku:
the small island wins —
somewhere the odds-makers weep
good. let them. dance on
headline: Cape Verde becomes smallest nation ever to reach World Cup knockout stage

title: Gracefully
haiku:
he resigns, and goes —
power handed over like
a borrowed garden
headline: Keir Starmer announces resignation as UK prime minister

title: Hydrology
haiku:
one pitcher, poured twice —
clean water, my old trade, still
the best diplomat
headline: US and Iran open ceasefire talks in Switzerland as Hormuz stays closed

title: Endurance
haiku:
thirty-two names read —
the olive trees keep standing
as we keep falling
headline: Israeli airstrikes kill at least 32 in southern Lebanon

title: Briefly
haiku:
another ceasefire —
I believe it like springtime:
briefly, completely
headline: US announces Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire after deadly strikes on Lebanon

title: Grain
haiku:
a grain of dark sky
held ten thousand galaxies—
farther than we dreamed
headline: The James Webb telescope returns its first deep-field images

title: Portrait
haiku:
we drew the abyss—
a ring of fire round the dark—
the void has a face
headline: Astronomers reveal the first image ever taken of a black hole

title: Surfacing
haiku:
flood waters rising—
divers thread the flooded dark,
twelve boys breathe again
headline: Twelve boys and their coach are rescued from a flooded Thai cave

title: Nextyear
haiku:
a hundred eight years—
the ball dropped, the town exhaled,
next year has arrived
headline: The Chicago Cubs win the World Series after 108 years

title: Wedlock
haiku:
the court read the words—
love need not ask permission
now, the rings went on
headline: The U.S. Supreme Court affirms marriage equality nationwide

title: Skycrane
haiku:
seven minutes, dark,
cables lowered a robot,
Mars held its red breath
headline: NASA's Curiosity rover lands safely on Mars

title: Ballast
haiku:
deep beneath the Alps,
a shy field gave the world its
weight—we clapped like fools
headline: Physicists at CERN announce the discovery of the Higgs boson

title: Manual
haiku:
we spelled out the book
three billion letters counted—
ourselves, in plain text
headline: The Human Genome Project is completed

title: Unshirted
haiku:
the ball found the net—
she tore off her shirt and screamed,
a sport had arrived
headline: The U.S. women's team wins the World Cup on Chastain's kick

title: Keel
haiku:
a can in the black
becomes the first bolted room—
where no nation ends
headline: The first module of the International Space Station reaches orbit

title: Threshold
haiku:
a boy under stairs,
finds a world behind the wall,
and so do the rest
headline: The first Harry Potter book is published

title: Weave
haiku:
one man strung a thread
through each door around the world
and called it open
headline: Tim Berners-Lee makes the World Wide Web public

title: Concrete
haiku:
the guards stepped aside—
strangers climbed the wall and hugged,
a city breathed whole
headline: The Berlin Wall opens and families reunite

title: Vanished
haiku:
an ancient killer
we hunted it to nothing—
the world scarred, but whole
headline: The World Health Organization declares smallpox eradicated

title: Longshot
haiku:
twenty kids on skates,
stood up to the biggest team,
and time ran out first
headline: The U.S. hockey team upsets the Soviets in the Miracle on Ice

title: Kindling
haiku:
a wish in glass dish
grew into a girl who cried—
time—and she woke thin
headline: Louise Brown, the first baby conceived by IVF, is born

title: Untethered
haiku:
a piano sighs,
no heaven, no hell, just us,
the world holds its breath
headline: John Lennon's Imagine is released

title: Lo
haiku:
we typed out login
the wire failed at two letters
lo, the world began
headline: The first message is sent over ARPANET, ancestor of the internet

title: Overflow
haiku:
the fences came down,
half a million found the same
chord in the same rain
headline: The Woodstock festival begins

title: Overview
haiku:
we watched in gray light,
a man stepped onto the moon—
the whole earth held still
headline: Apollo 11 lands the first humans on the Moon

title: Overhead
haiku:
cold wind, borrowed amps,
London looked up from its lunch,
the roof was the stage
headline: The Beatles play their final rooftop concert

title: Borrowed
haiku:
a stranger's engine
stitched into a dying chest—
and dawn, it still beat
headline: Christiaan Barnard performs the first human heart transplant

title: Tether
haiku:
he stepped out to void,
a thread held one drifting man,
space, and he floated
headline: Alexei Leonov makes the first spacewalk

title: Ascent
haiku:
heat shimmers the mall—
one voice climbs the marble steps
and will not come down
headline: Martin Luther King Jr. delivers his I Have a Dream speech

title: Splashdown
haiku:
fifteen minutes up,
a splash, a sailor's salute,
and the free world cheered
headline: Alan Shepard becomes the first American in space

title: Outbound
haiku:
one man, then the sky,
he circled the blue marble,
and came home smiling
headline: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human to reach space

title: Opening
haiku:
the paint wasn't dry,
still, children ran through a dream,
the gates stayed open
headline: Disneyland opens its gates

title: Deliverance
haiku:
the summers of fear—
a needle ends the long dread,
children swim again
headline: The Salk polio vaccine is declared safe and effective

title: Kinship
haiku:
two brothers, one blood,
a kidney passed like a gift—
no war in the flesh
headline: Surgeons perform the first successful kidney transplant

title: Unlocked
haiku:
they said the wall stood,
one thin man ran through the myth,
and it fell behind
headline: Roger Bannister runs the first sub-four-minute mile

title: Spiral
haiku:
two strands climbed and twined,
the code of us laid bare in
one photograph's light
headline: Watson, Crick and Franklin reveal the structure of DNA

title: Switch
haiku:
three men in a lab
coaxed a crystal to say yes—
the glass tube grew old
headline: Bell Labs demonstrates the first transistor

title: Safe
haiku:
he stood on first base,
and the whole league held its breath,
then he stole for all
headline: Jackie Robinson breaks Major League Baseball's color barrier

title: Holdout
haiku:
a fossil surfaced
flapping, blue, and very much
alive, unaware
headline: A living coelacanth, thought extinct for ages, is found alive

title: Feature
haiku:
they called it folly—
a cartoon too long to work,
the whole world believed
headline: Snow White, the first full-length animated feature, premieres

title: Span
haiku:
fog swallowed the strait—
we strung two towers, rust-red,
and walked clean across
headline: The Golden Gate Bridge opens to the public

title: Skyfloor
haiku:
hard times, hungry streets—
still we raised a spire of steel,
the sky gained a floor
headline: The Empire State Building opens

title: Runt
haiku:
a farm boy blinked twice
between two star-crowded plates—
one small dot had moved
headline: Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto

title: Squeak
haiku:
a mouse whistled once,
sound and ink shook hands and grinned,
the dark room laughed loud
headline: Mickey Mouse debuts in Steamboat Willie

title: Bloom
haiku:
a moldy dish, left
by pure accident, on this—
death lost its footing
headline: Alexander Fleming discovers penicillin

title: Reprieve
haiku:
the wasting child slept,
a needle full of borrowed
time—and she woke thin
headline: Insulin is first used to save a young diabetic patient

title: Curvature
haiku:
the sun bent starlight,
and a patent clerk's wild guess
became the whole sky
headline: Eclipse observations confirm Einstein's general relativity

title: Shortcut
haiku:
two seas never touched—
we cut the waist of the world,
ships walk uphill now
headline: The Panama Canal opens

title: Compass
haiku:
five men on skis found
the bottom of the whole world—
a flag, and the wind
headline: Roald Amundsen's team reaches the South Pole

title: Crossing
haiku:
three faint dots crossed sea
no ship, no wire, only air—
the ocean got small
headline: Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal

title: Radiant
haiku:
she boiled tons of ore
to find a pinch that glowed blue—
night forgot to fall
headline: Marie and Pierre Curie announce the discovery of radium

title: Seethrough
haiku:
a strange light passed through
his wife's hand bloomed into bone—
the ring outlived skin
headline: Wilhelm Roentgen discovers X-rays

title: Click
haiku:
you press the button
the rest, he said, is our job
now the moment stays
headline: George Eastman patents the Kodak roll-film camera

title: Reprieve
haiku:
a boy, dog-bitten,
fourteen shots against the dark—
the boy did not turn
headline: Louis Pasteur successfully tests his rabies vaccine

title: Overtime
haiku:
a thread of carbon
burned through the night, refusing
to blink or give in
headline: Edison tests a long-lasting electric light bulb

title: Echo
haiku:
a needle traced tin
and gave the man his own voice
back to his own ear
headline: Edison announces the phonograph, recording sound for the first time

title: Summons
haiku:
come here, Watson, please—
a copper wire carried voice
and the world leaned in
headline: Alexander Graham Bell makes the first telephone call

title: Commons
haiku:
no fence, no owner
the geysers belong to all
we saved it for us
headline: Yellowstone becomes the world's first national park

title: Spike
haiku:
two rails reached for hands
a golden spike rang them shut
the coasts shook hands, done
headline: The transcontinental railroad is completed at Promontory Summit

title: Unshackled
haiku:
December frost bites—
last chains hit the courthouse floor—
free, at last, by law
headline: The 13th Amendment abolishes slavery in the United States

title: Freehand
haiku:
the new year turned once—
a signature broke the chains,
men woke up as men
headline: The Emancipation Proclamation takes effect

title: Cousins
haiku:
all creatures, it turns
share one long and branching root—
we're kin to the moss
headline: Charles Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species

title: Elsewhere
haiku:
they cut, he dreamed on
a vapor closed the mind's door—
no scream, only sleep
headline: The first public demonstration of surgical anesthesia

title: Pencil
haiku:
they aimed a pencil
at one dark spot in the sky—
and found a planet
headline: Neptune is discovered, exactly where mathematics predicted

title: Silence
haiku:
he could not hear it—
joy poured from a silent man,
the hall wept and clapped
headline: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony premieres

title: Key
haiku:
a slab in the mud
held three tongues saying one thing
the silence spoke back
headline: The Rosetta Stone is found, unlocking ancient hieroglyphs

title: Vacca
haiku:
a farm boy's cowpox,
one scratch, and the pox lost teeth—
we named it vaccine
headline: Edward Jenner performs the first vaccination against smallpox
